heroHeadline: PNH Village de Dieu Offensive Day 5; MSF Cité Soleil Emergency Dept Reopens; OHCHR: 2,310+ Killed in 2026
heroSubtitle: The Haitian National Police continued its major Village de Dieu offensive through June 5, 2026 — the fifth consecutive day of operations against the 'Baz 5 Segonn' (5 Seconds) gang using armored vehicles, explosive drones, and tear gas. The offensive marks the first sustained police presence in the neighborhood in over five years and aims to reopen Route Nationale 2 to civilian traffic. On June 4, police deliberately destroyed a malfunctioning armored vehicle to prevent gang capture; on June 5, PNH issued a public safety warning urging civilians to avoid combat zones and alerting that gangs are using residents as human shields. The Gang Suppression Force (GSF), which formally launched full operations June 1, remains exclusively deployed in the city center (~800 personnel, ~15% of the 5,500-person authorized ceiling) and provides no coverage for Village de Dieu or Cité Soleil. On a humanitarian positive, MSF's Cité Soleil hospital emergency department and sexual violence care unit resumed operations as of June 1 — confirmed active June 4 — ending the acute phase of a 25-day forced closure. Full outpatient and inpatient services remain pending security stability; Cité Soleil has zero GSF coverage. OHCHR reported on June 4 that at least 2,310 people have been killed in Haiti from January 1 through June 4, 2026, with 699 women and girls subjected to documented sexual violence — an annualized pace approaching the 2024 record. The SCOTUS ruling on TPS for approximately 350,000 Haitian nationals (Trump v. Miot) remains pending, expected in late June–early July 2026.
